name: memory_purge
description: PHYSICALLY DESTROY a memory's content by ID. IRREVERSIBLE. Overwrites the memory's vector payload and stored text with zeros and removes it from every association graph. This is not the same as memory_forget: forget only sets a tombstone bit and every content byte stays readable on disk and in backups, whereas purge destroys the bytes and cannot be undone. Use forget for ordinary deletion; use purge only when the data itself must be gone, such as a data-subject erasure request. Purge does NOT reach DR exports, replica disks, cold-tier objects, filesystem snapshots or backups — copies there survive and must be handled separately. No cryptographic erasure is performed. Purge does not reclaim disk space; vacuum does that.

memory_id.description: The ID of the memory to physically destroy. This cannot be undone.

namespace.description: Target memory namespace (slug or ID). Omit to use connection or account default.
